test_cases.title: Compile-Time-Fixed Matrix Dimensions
test_cases.setup: Build the kmat library and unit-test binary on POSIX with template-instantiated matrix types of varying dimensions.
procedure: Instantiate kmat matrix types of dimensions 1x1, 3x3, 4x4, and 16x16 in the test translation unit.
Use static_assert to verify the row count, column count, and storage size of each instantiation are compile-time constants.
Use static_assert to verify sizeof(matrix) equals rows*cols*sizeof(element_type).
Compile the test; the static_assert must hold without runtime evaluation.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All static_assert checks pass at compile time, confirming dimensions and storage are fixed at compile time with no runtime size metadata.

test_cases.title: Matrix Multiplication - Square Matrices
test_cases.setup: Construct two 3x3 matrices A and B with known values and a 3x3 result matrix C.
procedure: Initialize A and B with hand-computed entries whose product is also hand-computed.
Invoke the kmat matrix multiplication operation C = A * B.
Compare each element of C against the hand-computed expected value within IEEE-754 rounding tolerance.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Every element of C equals the hand-computed expected product within 1e-9 absolute tolerance, and the operation returns a success status.

test_cases.title: Matrix Multiplication - Rectangular Compatible Dimensions
test_cases.setup: Construct a 2x3 matrix A and a 3x4 matrix B with known values, plus a 2x4 result matrix C.
procedure: Initialize A and B with hand-computed entries.
Invoke the kmat matrix multiplication operation C = A * B.
Compare each element of C against the hand-computed 2x4 expected product.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: C matches the hand-computed 2x4 product element-wise within 1e-9 tolerance.

test_cases.title: Matrix Transpose
test_cases.setup: Construct a 2x3 source matrix A with known values and a 3x2 destination matrix AT.
procedure: Initialize A with distinct values in each cell.
Invoke the kmat transpose operation AT = transpose(A).
Verify AT(j,i) == A(i,j) for every i in [0,rows) and j in [0,cols).
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Every element of AT equals the corresponding swapped-index element of A exactly (bit-equal floating point).

test_cases.title: Matrix Addition
test_cases.setup: Construct two 4x4 matrices A and B with known values and a 4x4 result matrix C.
procedure: Initialize A and B with distinct values per cell.
Invoke the kmat addition operation C = A + B.
Verify C(i,j) == A(i,j) + B(i,j) for every cell.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Every element of C equals the corresponding element-wise sum within 1e-12 absolute tolerance.

test_cases.title: Scalar Multiplication
test_cases.setup: Construct a 3x3 matrix A with known values and a 3x3 result matrix B.
procedure: Initialize A with distinct non-zero values.
Invoke the kmat scalar multiplication B = A * k for k = 2.5 and again for k = -1.0 and k = 0.0.
Verify B(i,j) == A(i,j) * k for each cell and each scalar.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Every element of B equals the corresponding A element times the scalar within 1e-12 tolerance for all three scalar values.

test_cases.title: Matrix Inversion - Identity Round-Trip
test_cases.setup: Construct a 3x3 invertible matrix A with known finite condition number.
procedure: Initialize A with values yielding determinant 1 (e.g., a known invertible test matrix).
Invoke the kmat inverse operation Ainv = inverse(A) and check return status.
Compute P = A * Ainv using the kmat multiplication operation.
Compare P against the 3x3 identity matrix element-wise.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Inverse returns success status and A * Ainv equals the identity matrix within 1e-9 absolute tolerance per element.

test_cases.title: Matrix Inversion - Known Numeric Inverse
test_cases.setup: Construct a 4x4 matrix A whose inverse is hand-computed and stored as expected_inverse.
procedure: Initialize A with hand-chosen values whose inverse is precomputed.
Invoke kmat inverse Ainv = inverse(A) and check return status.
Compare each element of Ainv against expected_inverse.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Each element of Ainv matches expected_inverse within 1e-9 absolute tolerance and the inverse returns success.

test_cases.title: Inversion Failure Status on Singular Matrix
test_cases.setup: Construct a 3x3 singular matrix S with a row of zeros (or two identical rows) so that det(S) == 0.
procedure: Initialize S as a known singular matrix.
Invoke the kmat inverse operation Sinv = inverse(S).
Inspect the returned status code.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The inverse operation returns a non-success failure status (e.g., JUNO_STATUS_ERR) and does not write a meaningful inverse.

test_cases.title: Inversion Failure Status on Near-Singular Matrix
test_cases.setup: Construct a 3x3 matrix N whose determinant is below the implementation's singularity threshold.
procedure: Initialize N with values producing a determinant of magnitude well below the singularity threshold (e.g., 1e-20).
Invoke the kmat inverse operation on N.
Inspect the returned status code.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The inverse operation returns a failure status indicating the matrix was treated as non-invertible.

test_cases.title: No Dynamic Allocation - Symbol Inspection
test_cases.setup: Build the kmat static library archive on POSIX with default optimization.
procedure: Run nm --undefined-only on the kmat archive (libjuno_kmat.a) and capture the output.
Programmatically grep the output for malloc, calloc, realloc, free, _Znwm, _Znam, _ZdlPv, _ZdaPv, mmap, sbrk, brk.
Assert the grep result is empty.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: The kmat archive references zero allocator symbols, confirming no dynamic memory allocation is used.

test_cases.title: Determinism - Repeated-Run Bit Equality
test_cases.setup: Prepare fixed input matrices for multiplication, addition, transpose, scalar-multiply, and inverse operations.
procedure: Run each operation on the fixed inputs and capture all output bytes via memcmp-friendly buffers.
Run each operation a second time and a third time on identical inputs in the same process.
Compare the three output buffers for each operation using memcmp.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: memcmp returns 0 for every pair of runs of every operation, confirming bit-identical results across repeated executions.

test_cases.title: POSIX vs Pico2 Numeric Equivalence
test_cases.setup: Capture golden output buffers for each kmat operation from a POSIX run; embed them as a header-included blob. The unit test compares the current build's outputs against the golden blob within IEEE-754 rounding tolerance, and the same test is run on the Pico2 target build via the cross-compiled test harness.
procedure: On POSIX, run all kmat operations against fixed inputs and capture outputs to a golden header.
On both POSIX and Pico2 builds, run the same operations and compare each output element against the golden values.
Assert each element matches within 1 ULP (or a documented tolerance equivalent to IEEE-754 single rounding).
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Both POSIX and Pico2 builds produce outputs that match the golden values within the documented IEEE-754 rounding tolerance.

test_cases.title: No Runtime Polymorphism - Symbol Inspection
test_cases.setup: Build the kmat static library archive with default flags.
procedure: Run nm on libjuno_kmat.a and capture all defined and undefined symbols.
Programmatically grep symbols for vtable markers (e.g., _ZTV, vtable for, _ZTI for typeinfo) and for any function-pointer-table style symbols inside kmat translation units.
Assert no vtable or typeinfo symbols originate from kmat objects.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: No vtable or typeinfo symbols are produced by kmat translation units, confirming static dispatch.

test_cases.title: 100 Percent Line Coverage of kmat Sources
test_cases.setup: Build the POSIX unit-test binary with --coverage flags and run all kmat tests; collect gcov data for libs/kmat_lib sources.
procedure: Run the kmat unit test suite with coverage instrumentation enabled.
Run gcov/lcov over libs/kmat_lib source files and produce a coverage summary.
Inspect the summary for line coverage percentage on each source file.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Reported line coverage is 100 percent for every source file under libs/kmat_lib (excluding test files themselves).

test_cases.title: Matrix Subtraction
test_cases.setup: Construct two 4x4 matrices A and B with known values and a 4x4 result matrix C.
procedure: Initialize A and B with distinct values per cell.
Invoke the kmat subtraction operation C = A - B.
Verify C(i,j) == A(i,j) - B(i,j) for every cell.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Every element of C equals the corresponding element-wise difference within 1e-12 absolute tolerance.

test_cases.title: No Runtime Type Information - Build Flag and Symbol Inspection
test_cases.setup: Build the kmat library and unit tests with -fno-rtti enforced via CMake compile options.
procedure: Programmatically inspect the CMake-generated compile_commands.json to assert -fno-rtti appears for every kmat compilation unit.
Run nm on libjuno_kmat.a and grep for _ZTI (typeinfo) and _ZTS (typeinfo name) symbols originating from kmat translation units.
Assert grep results are empty.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All kmat translation units are compiled with -fno-rtti and the produced archive has zero typeinfo symbols.

test_cases.title: No Thrown Exceptions - Build Flag and Symbol Inspection
test_cases.setup: Build the kmat library and unit tests with -fno-exceptions enforced via CMake compile options.
procedure: Programmatically inspect compile_commands.json to assert -fno-exceptions appears for every kmat compilation unit.
Run nm --undefined-only on libjuno_kmat.a and grep for __cxa_throw, __cxa_allocate_exception, __cxa_begin_catch, __cxa_end_catch, _Unwind_Resume, and __gxx_personality_v0.
Assert grep results are empty.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: All kmat translation units are compiled with -fno-exceptions and the archive references zero exception ABI symbols.

test_cases.title: Matrix Multiplication - Identity Element
test_cases.setup: Construct an arbitrary 4x4 matrix A and a 4x4 identity matrix I.
procedure: Compute B = A * I and C = I * A using the kmat multiplication operation.
Compare B and C against A element-wise.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: Both B and C equal A bit-exactly, confirming identity is the multiplicative neutral element.

test_cases.title: Transpose Involution
test_cases.setup: Construct a 3x4 matrix A with distinct values per cell.
procedure: Compute AT = transpose(A) and ATT = transpose(AT) using the kmat transpose operation.
Compare ATT against A element-wise.
test_cases.acceptance_criteria: ATT equals A bit-exactly, confirming transpose is an involution.
